I'm 53 this year, been farming these 15 mu for 30 years. Only finished primary school, but I know my land. I split it into 10 mu for wheat-maize double crop and 5 mu for cotton. My husband and son work in the county town — they send money home, but it means I'm mostly alone in the fields. I have to watch every yuan.

**Wheat (10 mu):** I'll plant around October 8th, right after the National Day holiday when my son can help for a day. I'm buying the same improved seed as last year from the shop in town — about 25 yuan per mu. For fertilizer, I'll put down 80 jin of compound fertilizer per mu before planting, then topdress with urea at jointing if the wheat looks yellow. That's roughly 12 kg of nitrogen per mu in total. I'll irrigate three times — winter water, return-green water, and grain-filling water. Each time the electricity meter runs fast, so I won't do more. I expect about 400 kg per mu. My neighbor Old Wang got 420 last year, but I don't want to risk spending more than him.

**Maize (10 mu):** Right after wheat harvest in early June, I have maybe five days to get the maize in the ground. I'll buy hybrid seed at 40 yuan per mu — can't save seed from last year, hybrid doesn't work that way. I'll put compound fertilizer in the hole at planting, about 60 jin per mu, then maybe add a bit of urea when the plants are knee-high. Around 11 kg nitrogen per mu. Two irrigations — one when it's jointing, one at tasseling. Summer rains might help, might not. I hope for 450 kg per mu. The turnaround is so tight I won't have time to till — just plant straight into the wheat stubble.

**Cotton (5 mu):** I'll plant in late April. I keep it to just 5 mu because picking is murder on your back, and I can't afford to hire too many hands. Seed costs 30 yuan per mu. I'll spread 70 jin of compound fertilizer per mu at planting — about 9 kg nitrogen — and that's it, no fancy split applications. Two irrigations, at flowering and when the bolls are filling. I'll need hired pickers for about 10 days total because my family can't do it all. I expect 240 kg of lint per mu if the bollworm doesn't hit too hard.

Money is tight. Fertilizer prices went up again. I'm spending almost 8,000 yuan on inputs this year — that's a lot for us. If something goes wrong, I'll have to borrow from my sister-in-law. But wheat and maize are my food security; I can't cut there. Cotton I might trim a little if cash runs short. Better to be safe than hungry.
